title: How review_ledger_task turns a bundle into a reviewable graph
head: 72c7ad3
summary: `review_ledger_task` opens a whole ledger task in the browser. The server reads the bundle from disk, turns each ticket's `**Blocked by:**` line into a dependency graph, checks that graph against the rules `to-tickets` writes by, and serves every other file only when the reviewer opens it. Every document reuses the Markdown reader, so the new ideas are three: reading ticket numbers out of prose, checking the graph, and evidence on demand.
primer:
A **ledger task** is a folder, `.ledger/<id>/`, that holds one piece of work. It always has `task.md` (intent, status, current state) and `retrospective.md`. Anything else is optional: a `spec.md` or `plan.md`, a `tickets/` folder, and whatever evidence the work produced, such as benchmark records or prototypes. Closed tasks move unchanged to `.ledger/history/<id>/`.

The `to-tickets` skill splits decided work into **tickets**, one file each, numbered in dependency order: `tickets/01-challenger-pass.md`, `tickets/02-trap-puzzles.md`, and so on. Each ticket follows one template:

```markdown
# 03: Benchmark runner and report

**What to build:** One command runs the trap benchmark …

**Blocked by:** 01 (Challenger pass), 02 (Three trap puzzles with reference solutions).

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] With the fake model and scripted replies, the command runs all three arms …
```

The **frontier** is every ticket whose blockers are all done: the work that can start now.
background:
Two pages already shared one runtime. A tool call builds the page's data, a small server on `127.0.0.1` serves it behind a token, and the tool call waits until the page posts its result to `/result`. The server then saves a self-contained copy of the page and returns the review to the model as text.

`review_markdown` added a **document reader**: the server splits a file into top-level blocks with their source lines, and the page lets the reviewer select text in a block and annotate it. Just before this change, that reader was made multi-document: every annotation now carries its `file`, so a page can hold many documents and still send back one list of annotations.

A ledger task is exactly that: many documents. What the reader cannot do alone is show how the tickets depend on each other, or deal with a bundle that holds 60 JSON records next to its four tickets.

steps.title: Reading ticket numbers out of prose
steps.body:
`**Blocked by:**` lines are written by people and agents, in many forms: `01: Title.`, `03 (Title)`, `01 (A), 02 (B).`, a Markdown link, `#04`. They also quote titles, and titles hold numbers of their own: "Retry 408 and 429 in phase 2".

Two patterns split the problem. `NUMBER` finds any two- or three-digit number, the way ticket numbers are written; a single digit is prose. `REFERENCE` finds only numbers that *read* as a reference: at the start of the line or of a list item, after `#`, `[`, `and`, or `ticket`.

```code components/browser-pages/src/tickets.ts:3-10
```

`parseTickets` combines them. A number that is a ticket of this bundle counts wherever it appears. A number that is *not* a ticket here counts only when it reads as a reference, and then it becomes an `unknown` blocker. So "Retry 408" is just a title, while "07: Report template" is a missing ticket the page should warn about.

```code components/browser-pages/src/tickets.ts:18-46
```

A ticket that names itself stays in its own `blockers` on purpose: the cycle check then catches it.

steps.title: Checking the graph
steps.body:
A ticket's state depends on the others. It is **done** or **in progress** by its own `Status:` line; otherwise it is **ready** only if every blocker is done *and* it names no missing ticket.

```code components/browser-pages/src/tickets.ts:52-58
```

`graphProblems` reports where the graph breaks the rules: an unknown blocker, a blocker numbered after the ticket it blocks (numbers follow dependency order), a cycle, and a graph where no ticket can start. The cycle search is a depth-first walk that marks a ticket *open* while it walks that ticket's blockers; reaching an open ticket again closes a loop.

```code components/browser-pages/src/tickets.ts:62-95
```

Both functions are pure and import nothing from Node, so the server uses them to read the bundle and the page imports the same code to colour the graph. One rule set, two places.

steps.title: Finding the bundle and its reading order
steps.body:
The agent passes `task` as whatever it has at hand: the id, `.ledger/<id>`, or a path inside the bundle. `bundleDir` tries the given path, then the id under `.ledger/`, then under `.ledger/history/`, and walks up from whatever exists to the folder directly under one of them.

```code components/browser-pages/src/ledger-review.ts:39-62
```

Documents come in the order a reviewer reads them: the task, its spec or plan, other documents, the tickets, the retrospective, then everything in folders. `[` and `]` in the page follow this order.

```code components/browser-pages/src/ledger-review.ts:74-82
```

steps.title: Evidence on demand
steps.body:
The page server gains one route. Like `/ask` and `/result`, it requires the token; unlike them, it is a `GET` that returns JSON, and it exists only when the tool passes a `file` handler.

```code components/browser-pages/src/page-server.ts:94-117
```

The ledger tool's handler is `serveEvidence`. It looks the path up in the page's own list, reads the file once, marks it binary if it holds a zero byte, and otherwise highlights its lines. The lines stay on the page object, which is why the saved copy shows every file the reviewer opened.

```code components/browser-pages/src/ledger-review.ts:130-143
```

Annotations on evidence point at lines (`l3`). The server accepts them only for a file it has served, so a submission cannot point at lines of a file nobody opened.

```code components/browser-pages/src/ledger-review.ts:147-157
```

steps.title: Laying out the graph
steps.body:
The page places each ticket in a column by its depth: tickets with no blockers in column 0, and every other ticket one column right of its deepest blocker. Within a column, tickets sort by the average height of their blockers, which keeps arrows from crossing. A cycle has no depth, so the `visiting` set breaks it and the back edge is drawn as a red loop under the graph.

```code components/browser-pages/web/ledger/graph.ts:15-54
```

steps.title: What the agent reads back
steps.body:
The result is plain text for the model. Every annotation names its file by repository path and lines, so the agent can open it directly; rewritten blocks come as before and after; and the documents the reviewer did not open are listed, so the agent knows what the approval did not cover.

```code components/browser-pages/src/ledger-review.ts:226-245
```

quiz.question: A ticket's line reads `**Blocked by:** 02: Retry 408 and 429 in phase 2.` The bundle holds tickets 01 to 05. What does the ticket wait on?
options: Nothing: the line quotes a title
quiz.why: 02 is a ticket of the bundle, so it counts wherever it appears. 408 and 429 are not tickets and do not read as references (they follow "Retry" and "and" mid-phrase), and a single digit such as 2 is prose.

quiz.question: Ticket 03 is `ready-for-agent`, and its only blocker is 07, which is not in the bundle. How does the page show 03?
options: Ready: nothing in the bundle blocks it
Blocked, and the graph checks report the missing 07
It is left out of the graph
quiz.why: A missing blocker cannot be known to be done, so `ticketState` returns blocked, and `graphProblems` reports that 03 waits on 07, which is not a ticket here.

quiz.question: Why does the server answer `GET /file` only for paths on the page's own evidence list?
options: So nothing holding the token can read files outside the bundle
Because the browser cannot send other paths
To keep the saved page small
quiz.why: The list is built by the server from the bundle folder. Answering only those paths means a request cannot name `../../.ssh/id_rsa` or any other file, even with the token.

quiz.question: A submission includes an annotation on line 3 of `evidence/run.json`, but the page never opened that file. What happens?
options: The server reads the file, then accepts it
quiz.why: Evidence lines are accepted only for a file the server has served (`blocksIn` returns nothing otherwise), and any malformed part rejects the whole submission.

quiz.question: Ticket 04 waits on 02 and 03. Ticket 02 waits on 01. Tickets 01 and 03 wait on nothing. Which column holds 04, counting from 0?
quiz.why: 01 and 03 have depth 0, 02 has depth 1, and 04 sits one column right of its deepest blocker, 02: column 2.
